record.original_question: Develop new Gronwall lemmas, both in concrete forms and in abstract forms.

evidence.quote: 10. The last two problems With the above considerations in mind look to the following problems: Problem 9. Give new concrete and abstract Gronwall lemmas.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall the classical Gronwall lemma: if $u, \beta : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ are continuous, $\alpha \ge 0$ is constant, and
$$u(t) \le \alpha + \int_a^t \beta(s)\, u(s)\, ds \qquad \text{for all } t \in [a,b],$$
then $u(t) \le \alpha \exp\!\left(\int_a^t \beta(s)\, ds\right)$ for all $t \in [a,b]$. Many extensions exist (Bihari, Bellman, Pachpatte, Wendroff, integral and discrete versions, versions on time scales, versions in ordered Banach spaces, fixed-point-theoretic abstract versions, etc.).

Problem. Formulate and prove genuinely new Gronwall-type lemmas, in both:
(a) Concrete form: explicit integral, sum, or functional inequalities yielding pointwise majorization of an unknown nonnegative function $u$ in terms of given data, with sharp or explicit bounds, going beyond the existing classical, Bihari, Pachpatte, Wendroff, time-scale, fractional, and stochastic variants.
(b) Abstract form: lemmas stated in ordered topological vector spaces, ordered Banach spaces, lattices, or via fixed-point principles (e.g. Perov-, Maia-, or Picard-operator type results), which yield as particular cases the classical and known generalized Gronwall inequalities.

Specifically: produce at least one new concrete inequality and one new abstract inequality, prove the corresponding bound, and demonstrate that the abstract version recovers the classical Gronwall lemma as a special case and is not equivalent to any previously published Gronwall-type result.
artifact.status_search_result: This is an open-ended research direction calling for the development of new Gronwall-type lemmas. It is inherently never fully "solved" in a binary sense, and the literature continues to produce new Gronwall-type inequalities (fractional, stochastic, time-scale, abstract Picard-operator forms). It remains an active area without a definitive resolution.

status_evidence.snippet: Lists ten open problems concerning Gronwall-type inequalities, including the call to develop new concrete and abstract Gronwall lemmas.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as one of ten open problems on Gronwall inequalities.
